card: bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0 is documented to disable timeouts, but currently fails immediately on macOS with 'Could not connect to the server'. A regression from PR 34342 caused the CLI to translate a zero timeout into a 5-year duration, exceeding macOS select() limit of 10^8 seconds and failing with EINVAL. This change caps durations in Sock::WaitMany to INT_MAX milliseconds and introduces an explicit Sock::NO_TIMEOUT sentinel passed directly to the underlying polling primitives. Unit tests are added to verify behavior with infinite and oversized timeouts.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the approach; provides the full diff and test cases matching the earlier version.
evidence: PR description: "`bitcoin-cli -rpcclienttimeout=0` is documented as 'no timeout', but on macOS it fails with 'Could not connect to the server' since #34342 (it's in v32.0rc1/rc2)."
PR description: "The new sock_tests/wait_large_timeout test waits with a 5 year timeout on a socket that already has data. It fails on master on macOS and passes with this change."
problem: Setting -rpcclienttimeout=0 in bitcoin-cli is documented to disable timeouts, but fails immediately on macOS and BSD systems with 'Could not connect to the server'. This happens because zero was mapped to a 5-year duration (~1.58 * 10^8 seconds), which exceeds the 10^8-second limit enforced by select() on macOS and returns EINVAL.

risk.why: A flaw in timeout calculations could cause socket operations in bitcoin-cli to block indefinitely or abort prematurely.

summary: Caps the timeout argument in Sock::WaitMany at INT_MAX milliseconds and introduces a Sock::NO_TIMEOUT constant that delegates to an infinite wait in poll() and select(). Updates bitcoin-cli to use this sentinel when -rpcclienttimeout is set to 0 instead of simulating an infinite wait with a 5-year timeout.
